issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise PerformanceWarning` is dead code.
issues.detail: The `break` statement immediately follows `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` inside the loop body — a raised exception unwinds the stack, so the break is never executed. All three reviewers flagged this as a tell that the author was undecided between warn-and-continue and fail-fast. Pick one posture and delete the other.

issues.description: Raising `PerformanceWarning` as an exception is a category error; contract is undecided.
issues.detail: `PerformanceWarning` is a Warning subclass, intended for `warnings.warn()`, not `raise`. The docstring says "performance warning," the code raises, and the PR description openly asks whether raising is appropriate — three different stories. The test then enshrines the wrong shape with `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning)`. Decide warn-and-proceed or rename to a real error (ValueError/RuntimeError) before merge.

issues.description: `safe_chunk_size` uses `max(1, itemsize)` to paper over an invariant that should be asserted.
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` defends against zero-itemsize dtypes that numpy never produces for real dtypes. Either the guard is dead and should be deleted, or it hides an unhandled case (object/structured dtypes) that deserves explicit handling. Write `z.dtype.itemsize * int(np.prod(zarr_write_chunks))` and assert the invariant.

issues.description: Divisibility check only inspects `dw[0]` per axis; uniform-chunks invariant is unstated.
issues.detail: The audit examines only the first chunk size on each axis, implicitly assuming `auto_chunks`/`normalize_chunks` returns uniform tuples. That assumption can break with ragged tail chunks and is nowhere documented. Either check every chunk on the axis, or state the invariant in a comment explaining why first-chunk is sufficient.

issues.description: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` is hostile to readers; write `!= 0`.
issues.detail: Python parses this correctly via precedence (`==` binds tighter than `not`), but a reader must stop and verify. `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:` is what's meant — one operator, obvious intent. Clarity over cleverness on a correctness guard.

issues.description: Test name `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` asserts `pytest.raises`, locking in the wrong contract.
issues.detail: The test name says "warns" but the body requires an exception via `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`. Once the warn-vs-raise contract is decided, either rename to `_raises` or switch the implementation to `warnings.warn` with `pytest.warns`. Test names are part of the literate record of intent.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously rates this PR NEEDS-WORK. The algorithmic intent — using shard shape as `previous_chunks` so `auto_chunks` produces shard-aligned chunks — is sound and the parametrized region-mode test is a real improvement. But the new misalignment-detection block has two P0 defects all three reviewers caught: an unreachable `break` after a `raise`, and raising a Warning subclass as a fatal exception while the docstring and PR description call it a warning. The contract is undecided — the author's own PR description asks whether raising is appropriate while the code already raises. Cleanup items: drop the `max(1, itemsize)` defensive paint, check all chunks per axis rather than only `dw[0]`, and rewrite the modulo guard as `!= 0`. Decide warn-vs-raise, fix the dead code, and the patch lands.
